text:
[IRET.7.6] Join tests may be evaluated in any order, and combine as
[LNUL.4.2]'s absorbing `and`: a test returning `false` rejects the pair
whatever another test raises — a trap, a `TypeError` or an `EngineError` — and
that fault reaches no surface ([LERR.1.4.11]). When no test is `false` and
several fault, the pair yields the one fault [LNUL.4.2]'s order selects. A token +
candidate fact pair passes the join only if all join tests
return `true`. The expression evaluation context provides
access to all fact pointers in the current (extended)
token plus the candidate fact in the "right" slot.

alloy.name: iret_7_6__conj
alloy.note: A conjunct: its outcome, whether it can raise by its declared types, nullability, and its body.

alloy.name: iret_9_5__v5_order_independent
alloy.note: ORDER INDEPENDENCE: every order gives one answer and records one atom, over every `where` of up to three conjuncts. A positional pick breaks it (TEETH). V5 as stated by [LNUL.4.2] and [IRET.9.5]: a false decides wherever it stands; otherwise the faults resolve by kind, then by the fields of the record (T2I); the evaluation order is free.

idris.name: Iret_7_6__env
idris.note: What a fact's key and payload ids stand for: a function from an id to the slot tuple it codes, or nothing. The model is quantified over it; the fixture runner supplies the decoder of the lowering's injective value code, so the engine's equality of ids is equality of slot values.

idris.name: iret_7_6__admits_join
idris.note: A positive node passes the pair only if the test answers true.

idris.name: iret_7_6__answer
idris.note: The answer a test gives the extended token.

idris.name: iret_7_6__blocks_join
idris.note: The negated node's relation. A trap BLOCKS under `no`. The clause blocks on true and on null and says nothing of a trap; blocking on it is the reading this model takes ('blocked unless false'), so this proves more than the clause states. The where fragment the Idris model runs produces no trap.

idris.name: iret_7_6__eval
idris.note: The evaluation context the clause describes -- every fact of the extended token plus the candidate -- over the fragment of Iret_7_5__expr, not over the whole expression language.

idris.name: iret_7_6__slot
idris.note: A slot of a fact of the extended token, the candidate last. A missing fact, an id the environment does not decode, or a missing slot reads as a trap: that is a lowering defect, not DS behaviour, and it surfaces in the Idris model as a missing firing rather than disappearing.

idris.name: iret_7_6__strict1
idris.note: A trap in the operand is raised.

idris.name: iret_7_6__strict2
idris.note: Operands are evaluated left first; a trap in the left is raised before the right is looked at.

idris.name: iret_7_6__joining
idris.note: The candidate facts of the right memory that pass every join test against the token.

idris.name: iret_7_5_1__probe_negated
idris.note: THE PROBE IS TRANSPARENT AT A `no` NODE when the anchor is decided on every candidate: the blockers found in the bucket are exactly the whole list's. Under `linear_scan: false` the condition holds by construction (`iret_7_5_1__typed_anchor_decided`); without it the probe is not transparent (`iret_7_5_1__null_anchor_escapes_probe`).

idris.name: iret_7_5_1__probe_positive
idris.note: THE PROBE IS TRANSPARENT AT A POSITIVE NODE, for an anchor wherever it stands in the test list: the bucket, tested by the other tests, is exactly what the whole list admits, traps included. The clause's 'probing on one first cannot change whether the pair passes'.

idris.name: iret_7_6__conj
idris.note: A node's tests combined: the absorbing `and` of their answers, true for none.

idris.name: iret_7_6__conj_pull
idris.note: A test WHEREVER IT STANDS in the list can be taken first: the combined answer is that test's `and` the rest's.

idris.name: iret_7_6__conj_test
idris.note: A node's test list as one test.

idris.name: iret_7_6__conj_test_pull
idris.note: The same for a node's test list, pair by pair.

idris.name: iret_7_6__map_append
idris.note: Answering a split list of tests is answering each part.

idris.name: iret_7_6__node_join
idris.note: The relation a node reads from its test: a positive node admits a pair answering true, a `no` node counts a candidate as a blocker unless it answers false. One test, two relations -- RLOW.5.3's 'the same join tests as the positive form'.

idris.name: iret_7_6__recompute_after_history_4
idris.note: THE VIEW THEOREM WITH FOUR-VALUED TESTS: after any history every alpha memory and every terminal of the loaded four-valued network is the recompute over working memory. The view theorem is over any relation, so this is its instance; the lemmas beside it say the relations are the clauses'.

idris.name: lnul_4_2__and_assoc
idris.note: The absorbing `and` is associative, traps included; with `lnul_4_2__and_commutes` a node's tests combine to one answer in any order.

idris.name: ltim_2_4_1__test_of
idris.note: A join test over the extended token with the candidate last, as Rete/Eval.idr's `iret_7_6__admits_join` evaluates it, with the clock leaves substituted first; the conjunction of a pattern's `within` and its `where` is one expression here, so [LNUL.4.2]'s absorbing `and` combines them.

idris.name: Iret_7_6__pair
idris.note: A pair a node's tests answer: rule ordinal, node position, token, candidate.

idris.name: iret_7_6__cross
idris.note: Every token against every candidate, at one node.

idris.name: Iret_7_6__conjunct
idris.note: One conjunct of a join: an outcome per (token, candidate).

idris.name: Iret_7_6__out
idris.note: What one conjunct yields for a pair: true, false, null, or a fault.

idris.name: iret_7_5_1__v5_probe_positive
idris.note: ANCHOR PROBING AT THE NETWORK: `iret_7_5_1__probe_positive` applied to V5 wheres -- probing on any one conjunct, then joining the rest, joins what the whole `where` joins at a positive node.

idris.name: iret_7_6__as_test
idris.note: A conjunct as a NetworkAnswer four-valued test.

idris.name: iret_7_6__map_fuse
idris.note: Answering the conjuncts as tests is projecting their outcomes.

idris.name: iret_7_6__v5_is_conj_test
idris.note: A V5 `where` IS NetworkAnswer's combined test of its conjuncts, pointwise: the four-valued network and its view theorem (`iret_7_6__recompute_after_history_4`), which quantify over every test, take V5 wheres unchanged.

idris.name: iret_7_6__v5_joining
idris.note: A node over a V5 `where` joins exactly what the node over NetworkAnswer's combined test joins.

idris.name: iret_7_6__v5_refines
idris.note: Projected onto answers, a V5 `where` is Rete/NetworkAnswer.idr's combined test `iret_7_6__conj`: the clause's 'passes only if all join tests return true', with every fault a trap.

idris.name: iret_7_6__v5_test
idris.note: A V5 `where` as a NetworkAnswer four-valued test. V5 as stated by [LNUL.4.2] and [IRET.9.5]: a false decides wherever it stands; otherwise the faults resolve by kind, then by the fields of the record (T2I); the evaluation order is free.

idris.name: lnul_4_2__v5
idris.note: A `where`'s answer under V5: its conjuncts combined by `and5`. V5 as stated by [LNUL.4.2] and [IRET.9.5]: a false decides wherever it stands; otherwise the faults resolve by kind, then by the fields of the record (T2I); the evaluation order is free.
